_about: OmegaWeapon Brand Stereopsis codebook. Two frames per target: the Sun eye is the brand's own voice (money pages, blog, press, social bios, GBP posts, ad copy the client supplied or the operator screenshotted); the Moon eye is the floor talking about the brand (reviews, forum and subreddit threads that name it, complaint databases, employer reviews, marketplace Q&A). Every counted item gets a topic (B01..B16), an optional topic2, an intent (Q C R H N D P J O, Horus codes), a stance (-1 0 1 from the customer's point of view) and flags (set, grey). The gap between the eyes per topic is the weighted log-odds z (Monroe, Colaresi and Quinn 2008), computed in scripts/omega_metrics.py, never typed by hand. Reviews are one item each; a review platform's aggregate count is a Nilometer signal, not an item. Reviewer and poster names are never recorded.

topics.label: Service quality and outcome
topics.def: Whether the job, product or result was good; workmanship, accuracy, effectiveness, taste, fit.

topics.label: Price, value and billing
topics.def: Cost, quotes, surprise charges, invoices, refunds, financing terms, value for money.

topics.label: Speed and responsiveness
topics.def: How fast they answered, showed up, shipped, delivered or resolved; wait times and delays.

topics.label: Staff and people
topics.def: Named roles (technician, nurse, attorney, rep) and how they treated the customer; courtesy, knowledge, attitude.

topics.label: Credentials, trust and safety
topics.def: Licenses, certifications, insurance, awards, years in business, scam or fraud accusations, safety.

topics.label: Location, hours and availability
topics.def: Where they are, service area, hours, appointment availability, capacity, parking, accessibility.

topics.label: Booking, intake and process friction
topics.def: Forms, phone trees, scheduling systems, paperwork, checkout, account setup, cancellation steps.

topics.label: Communication and follow-up
topics.def: Being kept informed, callbacks, explanations, updates, ghosting after the sale.

topics.label: Guarantees, warranties and promises
topics.def: Stated guarantees, warranty claims and whether promises were honored.

topics.label: Reputation talk and reviews about reviews
topics.def: Items about the reviews themselves: fake review accusations, review requests, incentives, response to reviews, ratings.

topics.label: Promotions, offers and marketing
topics.def: Discounts, coupons, seasonal offers, ads seen, mailers, marketing tone, spam.

topics.label: Product, catalog and selection
topics.def: The thing itself when it is a product or menu: selection, stock, quality of goods, sizing, materials.

topics.label: Technology, app and digital experience
topics.def: The website, app, portal or tech used in service; bugs, ease of use, features, online tools.

topics.label: Complaints, disputes and compliance
topics.def: Formal complaints, chargebacks, legal threats, regulator or BBB filings, licensing disputes, contract disputes.

topics.label: Hiring, workplace and culture
topics.def: Employee and applicant voice: pay, management, culture, turnover, job postings.

topics.label: Other
topics.def: Items about the brand that fit no topic above; the Other share is a measure of frame noise.

sun_frames: homepage and money pages (the raw fetcher's text)
blog or news hub, latest 20 posts
press releases and media mentions the brand links to
ad copy from library screenshots or the client's exports
moon_frames: Google reviews (screenshots or the client's GBP export; the panel is not fetchable)
Yelp, Trustpilot, BBB, Angi, Avvo, Healthgrades, G2 or the vertical's review site (screenshots or exports)
App Store review RSS (fetchable) and Play reviews (screenshots)
Reddit, forums and Q&A threads naming the brand (search snippets and titles only; author never recorded)
CFPB complaint API rows for the company (public endpoint)

reading_the_gap.floor-led: Customers talk about it more than the brand does: usually pain the site does not address, or a strength the site fails to claim.
reading_the_gap.broadcast-led: The brand leads on it and customers do not echo it: unproven claims, or a message that is not landing.
reading_the_gap.floor-only: The brand is silent on something customers raise; a content and reputation gap at once.
reading_the_gap.broadcast-only: The brand's talking point has no echo; check whether it is true before repeating it in ads.

minimums.note: Below the minimums the tab still renders, the counts show beside every share, and the Brief's coverage strip says the read is thin.
